findings.summary: `<title>`/`<textarea>` content is serialised verbatim like raw-text `<script>`/`<style>`, so decoded character references re-emit as live markup (sanitizer bypass)
findings.description:
## Status **Fixed in the working tree (unreleased).** The serialiser now routes ``/`<textarea>` through the escapable-raw-text path — `&`, `<`, `>` (and U+00A0) are re-escaped, and only the true raw-text elements `<script>`/`<style>` are written verbatim (`dom.go`). The parity case `parse-raw-text` now matches the cheerio oracle, and `Page.HTML()`/`NormalizedHTML()`/`Element.OuterHTML()`/`InnerHTML()` round-trip escapable-raw-text content safely. **v0.2.0 remains affected** because the fix has not yet been published; this finding is retained for the coordinated release of that fix. See `puppeteer/API-DEVIATIONS.md`. ## Affected `github.com/malcolmston/puppeteer` **<= 0.2.0** (v0.2.0 is the only published release; the fix is in the working tree but not yet released). Parity cases: `parse-raw-text`, `parse-full-document`, `http-page-html` (harness findings **P8/P9** and **H2** in `parity/puppeteer/COVERAGE.md`). Oracle: `cheerio@1.0.0` (parse5 + dom-serializer). Affected output paths, all sharing one root cause in the serialiser: `Page.HTML()`, `Page.NormalizedHTML()`, `Element.OuterHTML()`, `Element.InnerHTML()`. ## Mechanism Ordinary text nodes are escaped **correctly** and round-trip fine — `escapeText` turns `&`→`&`, `<`→`<`, `>`→`>`, so a `<div>` (or `<p>`, `<span>`, …) holding text that came from decoded character references is re-emitted safely. The defect is narrower and more dangerous. The serialiser (`dom.go`) puts the HTML **"escapable raw text"** elements — `<title>` and `<textarea>` — in the *same* verbatim branch as the true **raw-text** elements `<script>` and `<style>`: ```go // dom.go var rawTextElements = map[string]bool{"script": true, "style": true} var escapableRawText = map[string]bool{"textarea": true, "title": true} ... case TextNode: if p := n.Parent; p != nil && p.Type == ElementNode && (rawTextElements[p.Data] || escapableRawText[p.Data]) { sb.WriteString(n.Data) // <-- written VERBATIM, no escaping } else { sb.WriteString(escapeText(n.Data)) } ``` Writing `<script>`/`<style>` verbatim is correct (their content is CDATA-like and re-tokenised literally). Writing `<title>`/`<textarea>` verbatim is **not**: they are *escapable* raw text, so the parser **decodes character references inside them** on the way in, and the serialiser must **re-escape** `&` and `<` on the way out. Because it does neither, both `&` and `<` leak, turning what was escaped, inert text back into live markup — a sanitizer bypass. ## Upstream vs port Source `<textarea></textarea><script>alert(1)</script></textarea>` — the escaped text of a comment/handle that should stay *inside* the textarea: | | re-serialised | | --- | --- | | upstream (cheerio 1.0.0 / parse5) | `<textarea></textarea><script>alert(1)</script></textarea>` — references re-escaped, the `</textarea>` and `<script>` stay inert text | | this port | `<textarea></textarea><script>alert(1)</script></textarea>` — the `</textarea>` **closes the textarea early** and the following `<script>` becomes **live markup** | The same escaped content placed in a `<div>` is serialised **correctly** by the port (it goes through `escapeText`), which pinpoints the bug to the `escapableRawText` verbatim branch rather than to text handling in general. The plain-`&` case (`<title>Doc & Title` → `Doc & Title`) is the mild symptom of the same branch. ## Impact (attacker terms) Serialisation is the boundary where a DOM becomes markup again. Content that was **inert, escaped text inside a `` or `<textarea>` in the source document comes back out live**. A scrape → cache → render pipeline built on `Page.HTML()` therefore converts harmless escaped user content that appears inside a `<textarea>`/`<title>` on a third-party page into a closed element followed by live script in its own output — a **stored-XSS-enabling sanitizer bypass**: whoever controls that page's user content can inject `<script>` (or any markup) into the consumer's origin. Round-tripping is not idempotent, the usual signature of an unsafe serialiser. Impact is contingent on the consuming application rendering or forwarding the serialiser output as HTML — the normal use of the API, but one step removed from direct script execution. **It only bites once the output is rendered as HTML.** ## Reproduction ```go const src = `<!doctype html><html><head><title>Doc & Title` + `` + `
<script>alert(2)</script>
` srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html; charset=utf-8") fmt.Fprint(w, src) })) defer srv.Close() b, _ := puppeteer.Launch(puppeteer.LaunchOptions{}) p, _ := b.NewPage() p.Goto(srv.URL) fmt.Println(p.HTML()) ``` Observed — the `
<script>alert(2)</script>
... ``` Expected (what parse5/cheerio produce) — the `
<script>alert(2)</script>
... ``` ## Suggested fix Serialise `` and `<textarea>` through the escapable-raw-text path, **not** the raw-text path: escape `&`→`&` and `<`→`<` (and U+00A0→` `) in their text, escaping `&` first. Only true raw-text elements (`script`, `style`) may be written verbatim. The `escapableRawText` set must be dropped from the verbatim branch of `Node.render`. ## Severity rationale Graded **high**. This is not a cosmetic escaping quirk: because `<title>`/`<textarea>` are serialised verbatim while the parser decodes references inside them, escaped attacker text is re-emitted as live markup, giving a **sanitizer bypass that enables stored XSS** in any consumer that renders `Page.HTML()`/`OuterHTML()` output as HTML. The one mitigating factor — impact is realised only once the output is rendered/forwarded as HTML, which is the normal use of the API — is why it is graded high rather than critical, not medium.
